lecture_title: Proper Time, Time Dilation, and Length Contraction

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: Stanford title card with no mathematical or diagrammatic content.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This program is brought to you by Stanford University.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: Shows the Galilean transformation and the initial spacetime axes while the moving-frame grid is being constructed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: On the same graph, draw the t prime axis.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: Clearly identifies the moving clock's worldline as x=vt, x'=0, and the t' axis during the time-dilation derivation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: His trajectory is x equals vt.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: Replacement frame shows the compact-cylinder construction at the actual point of the global-identification question.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Imagine that space is a cylinder.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The complete Lorentz transformation is visible with the factors of c restored.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Now it makes good dimensional sense.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: Shows the null-coordinate combinations and reciprocal boost factors used to explain the light-cone squeeze.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: T plus x gets stretched or squeezed.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: Captures the completed cancellation proving invariance of t squared minus x squared.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: Shows the light cone at the transition among timelike, lightlike, and spacelike separation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This is called the timelike region.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: The moving-clock calculation and final time-dilation factor are legible together.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That is the famous formula of time dilation.
assets.caption_hint: Time dilation from the invariant interval

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: Shows both twin worldlines and the proper-time algebra after the outward and return legs have been combined.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The smaller proper time is associated with the twin who went away.
assets.caption_hint: Twin paths and elapsed proper time

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: Preserves the completed exchange of light pulses used to compare what each twin actually receives.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Signals that the stationary observer sees.
assets.caption_hint: Light signals exchanged between the twins

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: Shows the rod's worldsheet and the tilted constant-t' slice defining a simultaneous moving-frame length measurement.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The length is the interval between the two ends at the same time.

assets.name: lecture_04_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: Shows the completed spacelike-interval calculation and the contracted length of a unit rod.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The stationary meter stick is seen to be shortened.
